topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: PAMPs, DAMPs, and self versus non-self recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the principles and molecular criteria used by the innate immune system to detect infection and tissue damage through PAMPs and DAMPs.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families and signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genetics, cellular localization, and downstream signaling cascades of pattern recognition receptors, including Toll-like receptors and inflammasomes.

topics.label: Leukocyte recruitment, trafficking, and systemic inflammatory responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how sentinel cell activation directs leukocyte recruitment into tissues, adaptive immune priming via lymphatics, and the systemic consequences of excessive inflammation.

topics.label: Inflammation resolution, tissue repair, and chronic containment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inflammation is terminated and repaired, as well as the chronic tissue outcomes and granuloma formation that occur when resolution fails.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic wraps up the lecture and introduces the next topic on the complement system.
